items.article_search_text: There's still plenty to play for in the final three rounds of the season, with the fight for second in the standings wide open. Read more at foxsports.com.au. The high-profile Las Vegas Grand Prix fires the starting gun on three races in three weeks to close the 2026 season with plenty still to play for. The finish line is in sight for Formula 1 in 2026. After 20 rounds of racing, just three grands prix remain, beginning with this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix. Formula 1 first conquered the Las Vegas Strip, shutting the neon-lit road for racing, three years ago in a highly hyped sporting coup. Watch the final 3 qualifying sessions in the 2026 F1® season Live and Free with Kayo Freebies. Watch FORMULA 1 HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX 2026 qualifying session on Saturday 21st November > Though the race has to some extent become part of the furniture after three grands prix, it remains among the highest profile events on the calendar for the sheer audacity of its location. Fortunately the track and the chilly night-time desert climate have a history of producing reliably good racing. Though the headline championship results are already settled, the final triple-header of the year — and unhinged combination of races that will see the sport fly more than 13,000 km to Qatar immediately after the chequered flag — has plenty still at stake. PIT TALK PODCAST: We look ahead to the beginning of the end of the Formula 1 season with this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix in one of the sport’s all-time great time zones, and it’s match point for Marc Márquez at this weekend’s MotoGP Portuguese Grand Prix. | Listen to Pit Talk below. CAN MERCEDES GET RUSSELL TO SECOND PLACE? Mercedes has won the constructors championship, and with Andrea Kimi Antonelli it’s won the drivers title too. But this glittering season isn’t complete with three rounds remaining. Mercedes wants a one-two championship finish. That means sneaking George Russell into second place. “Our targets are clear: helping George finish as high as possible in the drivers’ championship, ending the year with momentum, and continuing to unlock more performance from the car,” Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said. But while Antonelli has taken the title at a canter, Russell has lagged behind. He dropped to third several times during the European leg of the season and plummeted to fourth after the Mexico City Grand Prix. He’s now third but 17 points behind Max Verstappen for second. He’s also only one point clear or Lewis Hamilton in fourth. Drivers championship, battle for second Max Verstappen: 279 points George Russell: -17 points Lewis Hamilton: -18 points Charles Leclerc: -30 points Lando Norris: -33 points It’s far from an insurmountable gap, but Verstappen is in obviously better form. The Dutchman is on an eight-round podium streak and has won three of the last five grands prix. Russel’s last podium was his victory in Azerbaijan in September. It’s raised the prospect of Mercedes giving him a leg-up, perhaps even with a team orders advantage. “It could be a possibility that we’re giving it all the force,” Wolff hinted in Brazil. It would be a bizarre situation, the new champion giving up results to help who was his chief title rival to second place. Even just the prospect of team orders to secure a minor place on the title table is novel. Of course Mercedes hasn’t said that team orders will be used, and it’s hard to believe the team would lack self-awareness to such a degree that Antonelli might be asked to give up a victory or a podium to help Russell. Russell surely wouldn’t want a result handed to him like that anyway. For the let-down Englishman, it’s more important that he finish the season in good form than with a higher championship position. “For me what’s more important is just to have some strong weekends,” he said. “That doesn’t necessarily just mean the result; it just means from FP1 through the weekend showing good performances. “This season has been so up and down even during the weekend — even my strong weekends, other than Baku, sometimes it hasn’t been every lap of the weekend. “Of course I’d love to finish as high as possible, but that’s the most important thing.” The importance of finishing second, however, has prompted Russell not to use Mercedes’s upgraded turbocharger, which is making its debut this weekend, as using the new part would incur a grid penalty. Antonelli and multiple other Mercedes drivers will use the better turbo, though the team itself says the expected benefit is only minor. WHAT CAN PENALISED PIASTRI ACHIEVE? McLaren is bringing an upgraded car to this weekend, and Oscar Piastri will have to wield it to its maximum if he’s to get a big result. Piastri will start with one hand tied behind his back with a grid penalty for taking a new internal combustion engine, sending him 10 places down the order. He’ll also get the benefit of Mercedes’s new turbocharger, though this will come without penalty for him. With an average qualifying result of 6.4 this season, the Australian is likely to start around 16th on the grid. What he can achieve from well outside the points remains to be assessed through the practice sessions. “Just trying to maximise what we can do; we don’t know exactly where we’re going to sit with things,” he said. “Hopefully the new engine is going to help out a little bit — there are obviously going to be some spots to make up. “We’ll learn as much as we can about the race through practice — also I think we learned a lot in Monza about what qualifying could look like and the slipstreams and tows that people are going to want. “It’s going to be a pretty interesting qualifying session as well as race.” MORE FORMULA 1 ‘DOWN TO THE WIRE’: McLaren targets $15m payday… and Piastri’s form will be crucial PIT TALK: F1's newest team makes call on final 2027 seat; legend set for rally switch VEGAS RETROSPECTIVE: A catastrophic blunder turned Vegas into a 'horror movie'. McLaren is still paying the price What we do know ahead of time, though, is that Las Vegas is historically a weak McLaren circuit, and it isn’t expected to suit the car any better this weekend. The McLaren car doesn’t like short, slow corners or long straights, but that’s pretty much all there is in Las Vegas. The track has a similar profile to Azerbaijan, where the car was 0.8s off the pace. Paradoxically, though, Baku was actually one of Piastri’s stronger weekends, having been on for a podium before the race unravelled late. It was the first in a run of races in which Piastri has felt himself getting more comfortable in the car. “I think in general it’s been looking a bit better recently,” he said. “Austin and Mexico maybe not quite so much, but I felt like through Malaysia, Singapore, Baku and then Brazil as well the results maybe weren’t always what they could’ve been on those weekends, but the feeling in the car was definitely an improvement. “[In Brazil] qualifying was a shame because the pace I had on Sunday was the strongest it’s been for a while. “That’s the big positive. It’s just about trying to convert that potential now into results.” It's important to McLaren that Piastri finds form as it seeks to overhaul Red Bull Racing for third in the constructors championship, but good form might be enoguh for only minor points this weekend. HAMILTON DENIES FERRARI TRUST PROBLEMS There’s no denying Lewis Hamilton has had a strong season — a far, far stronger season than he had last year — but his more competitive campaign has uncovered deep cracks in Ferrari as a title-challenging prospect. The power unit isn’t up to scratch, but that’s part of the game to some extent. The executional errors have been more painful but at least explainable in the context of this being a deeply inexperienced Ferrari team — the Scuderia hasn’t won a championship in almost two decades. But the appearance of conflict and tension between Hamilton and Charles Leclerc has been harder to handle. More problematic still is what looks like trust issue between Hamilton and his team. In Singapore and in Brazil — twice in the last four grands prix — Hamilton disobeyed orders to pit for fresh tyres, appearing to believe he could better dictate strategy from the cockpit. On both occasions it backfired. In Singapore he tumbled out of podium contention, and in Brazil he spun off the track in the wet. Hamilton wouldn’t be the first driver to lack faith in Ferrari’s strategy calls, but the seven-time champion didn’t so much argue as he did unilaterally ignore the calls to the detriment of both the team and to his standing in the drivers championship. Speaking Las Vegas, Hamilton denied he and Ferrari had trust issues but admitted more work had to be done to hone the team collectively. "We're constantly working on our communication," he said, per the BBC. "It's been a lot better this year. Carlo [Santi, Hamilton’s new race engineer] has done an amazing job, and those particular two times [in Singapore and Brazil], particularly the last time, was just I didn't have the information I needed. I got the call right at the last minute. "We'll just continue to work on the processes. We're super united in what's working, in the right direction." In the context of Mercedes having been destined to control both championships this season, Ferrari’s 2026 can be written off as a crucial learning year — learning not only about the new rules but also about how to handle a competitive line-up with Hamilton alongside Charles Leclerc. But the team has only three races remaining to iron out these problems before the 2027 acid test begins. STROLL HOMES IN ON UNWANTED RECORD Lance Stroll is on the cusp of one of Formula 1’s most unwanted records: most DNFs in a single season. Because this is motorsport, the record is more complicated than you might think. Andrea de Cesaris holds the record for most failures to finish in a season. In the 1987 season, he failed to finish every single one of the 16 rounds. However, though he didn’t see the chequered flag at any race, he was classified twice for having completed 90 per cent of the race distance before running into problems. One of those two classifications was the Belgian Grand Prix, where he remarkably finished third in a race that saw a sensational 24 of 26 drivers fail to make the finish. The alternative record is most non-classifications — what we would usually describe as a DNF (did not finish). De Cesaris also holds the record for most non-classifications in a season with the 14 DNFs he accrued in 1987. Where does Stroll stand against these benchmarks? The Canadian has 13 DNFs for the season. However, he was also not classified at the Australian Grand Prix for not having completed 90 per cent of the race despite seeing the chequered flag — he spent 15 laps in his garage due to problems with his car and engine, too many to be included in the results. Therefore he’s already equalled De Cesaris’s 14-race record for non-classifications. One more would see him hold the record outright. The break the record for non-finishes, however, he would have to retire from all of the remaining three grands prix this season. Of course the significantly longer season has ‘helped’ his cause here. De Cesaris will almost certainly always hold both records on a percentage basis. But modern F1 is also far more reliable than in the days of De Cesaris’s famously problem-prone career, which saw him retire from a staggering 146 races in his 208-start career — a non-finishing rate of 70.2 per cent. The sheer number of retirements, therefore, is still impressive. “I heard about it,” Stroll said of the record. “We’ve had a lot of issues out there, a lot of engine problems. “It’s been a tough year for the whole team. New Delhi: Australia's Formula 1 driver Oscar Piastri weighed in on the revived Sandpapergate episode, which has caught Australian cricket in choppy waters following Usman Khawaja's recent revelations.Khawaja, a former Aussie cricketer, revealed in his book, Sabr, that the entire Australian team was aware of the ball-tampering plans in the infamous 2018 Cape Town Test and that they also implemented them in the previous match in Port Elizabeth.Piastri, who is himself a big cricket fan, was asked about his statement on the same ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, and he felt "it is not really a nice thing" for it to re-emerge in the headlines and hoped that it could be dealt with quickly."It has obviously been an interesting couple of weeks, that is for sure with what has been unfolding," Piastri said, as quoted by Australia's The Daily Telegraph."I know quite a few of the guys involved personally, so it is not really a nice thing to see it being brought back up necessarily, but it is what it is."Obviously I’ve got no knowledge, and I remember when it happened eight years ago, but I think for everyone, especially the Australian cricket community and Australia as a country, the quicker it can be dealt with, whatever that looks like, the better," he added.Piastri is himself a cricket fan, having previously worn Brett Lee's ODI jersey in the paddock, and he also has a picture of himself standing next to former cricketer Ricky Ponting from when he was a child.He also hosted Aussie stars Nathan Lyon, Mitchell Starc and Usman Khawaja at the McLaren Technology Centre in England ahead of the WTC 2025 final. "I know myself as a sports person that the noise around certainly is not going to be helpful, so the quicker it can be resolved and put behind us, the better for everyone," Piastri added on the saga.The Sandpaper scandal is fresh in the headlines, with differing opinions coming from all sides. Following Khawaja's claims, David Warner backed his former teammate, calling his statement "100% accurate".Current captain Pat Cummins, who was among the bowling group during that Test match, hit back at Khawaja, saying that his statement is "complete and utter nonsense".Cameron Bancroft, the on-screen implementer of the sandpaper, issued his statement in a 4000-word article in the West Australian, where he claimed that the "whole team" knew about the use of the sandpaper during the 2018 South Africa series and also that he "did not give a complete and truthful account" when he was investigated by Cricket Australia in the aftermath of the scandal. The scandal led Australia to hand Bancroft a nine-month ban, along with a year-long ban each to Warner and Steve Smith.

items.article_search_text: Oscar Piastri faces a 10-place grid penalty at the 2026 Las Vegas GP as McLaren introduces upgrades and Google launches an F1 collectibles auction. Formula 1's 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix race week is bringing significant developments both on and off the track, with Oscar Piastri facing a 10-place grid penalty, McLaren preparing technical upgrades, and Google opening a special collectibles auction for fans from November 18 to 20 in Las Vegas.According to McLaren's race preview, Piastri will start with a grid penalty after exceeding his permitted allocation of internal combustion engines. Meanwhile, discussions about Formula 1's future power units and exclusive fan experiences are adding to the attention surrounding the event.FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem indicated that the championship could eventually return to V8 engines through a social media announcement. An earlier post published by the FIA suggested that an agreement in principle had been reached with Formula 1 teams for a potential introduction in 2030, but the post was subsequently deleted.Ben Sulayem retained a separate message on his personal account, writing: "The people spoke. We listened. V8s. Coming soon," alongside an audio clip featuring the engine sound.V8 engines last appeared in Formula 1 in 2013, before the championship transitioned to 1.6-liter V6 power units. Although Ben Sulayem has previously mentioned 2030 as a possible return date, his remaining social media statement did not specify a year.McLaren confirmed that Piastri will receive a new internal combustion engine in Las Vegas following a reliability issue. Because this will be his fifth engine of the season, the Australian driver must serve a 10-place grid penalty.The team explained the decision in its race preview: "Oscar will take a new Internal Combustion Engine in Las Vegas after a reliability issue. As it is his fifth of the season, he will take a 10-place grid penalty, but he has a good chance to recover positions with overtaking in Saturday's race."McLaren also confirmed that both cars will receive an updated turbo specification enabled by the Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities system. The team expects only a relatively small performance improvement from the component.The team's statement added: "Both cars, as with the other HPP-powered cars, will be fitted with a new ADUO-enabled turbo specification: the expected performance benefit is relatively small."Further improvements are planned for the MCL40, including a revised floor. The development follows McLaren's previous upgrades in Brazil, where Lando Norris secured victory in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.Ross Hood, McLaren's Executive Director of Programme Delivery, described the latest development as an example of coordinated work across several departments.Hood said: "A new floor is arriving in Las Vegas this week, and it's a great example of our programme delivery."He also highlighted the contribution of the team's technical and manufacturing departments. Their cooperation helped McLaren maximize the results of its latest wind tunnel development work for the 40A specification.Google is also using the Las Vegas Grand Prix to introduce The Auction by Google Play, an interactive event running at The Aria Hotel from November 18 through November 20. Admission is free, while Google Play Points members receive priority access and additional benefits.Visitors can collect auction tokens by using a large interactive machine. Those tokens can be exchanged for customized keepsakes, including keychain charms and personalized 3D-printed race cars.The auction's featured collectibles include a wall-mounted replica of the 2026 McLaren Racing livery halo device and a customized Google Play collaboration jacket designed with Jeff Hamilton. Auctioneer Phyllis Kao is scheduled to lead the main auction on November 20 at 7 p.m. Pacific Time.Google Play Points members in the United States can also access exclusive digital rewards. Available items include a signed Lando Norris bucket hat, a 2026 Lando Norris 1:2 Silverstone mini helmet, and a Google Play collaboration toolbox with Toyo.Members in the Gold Plus tier can unlock a digital rewards case through the Google Play application, with opportunities to receive points boosters and physical collectibles. Other membership tiers can redeem accumulated points for selected limited-edition merchandise.

items.article_search_text: McLaren is hoping its 2027-focused upgrades in Las Vegas could give it an edge over Red Bull Racing — but Oscar Piastri will have to play his part. Read more at foxsports.com.au McLaren is all-in on beating Red Bull Racing to third in the teams title — but unlike last year, it doesn’t think it needs to sacrifice 2027 to do it. McLaren started the season as the defending champion. With three rounds remaining in 2026, it’s fighting to avoid a fourth-place finish — last in the frontrunning class. The team has spent almost all season in third place, its lead over the struggling Red Bull Racing peaking at a comfortable 83 points after the Italian Grand Prix. But it’s been all one-way traffic since then. McLaren was outscored by almost 17 points per weekend over the following five rounds until it was tied with Red Bull Racing on 355 points after the United States Grand Prix, where it fell to fourth place on countback. Watch the final 3 qualifying sessions in the 2026 F1® season Live and Free with Kayo Freebies. Watch FORMULA 1 HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX 2026 qualifying session on Saturday 21st November > The margin now stands at 17 points, with momentum having swung decisively towards Red Bull Racing. That Lando Norris won in Brazil only somewhat stemmed the bleeding. Max Verstappen’s monumental 20th-to-second performance underlined who holds the whip hand in this lucrative battle for minor placing. With millions of dollars on the line — never mind the pride of two teams who have shared the last four constructors titles — the next three weeks are significant ones for McLaren and Red Bull Racing. IT ALL STARTED LAST YEAR It’s no surprise that these two teams find themselves locked in a battle to avoid a last-in-class finish this season. We’ve seen this story so many times: the title-contending teams in the final season of a regulation set overcommit to the outgoing rules and find themselves undercooked for the new era. PIT TALK PODCAST: We look ahead to the beginning of the end of the Formula 1 season with this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix in one of the sport’s all-time great time zones, and it’s match point for Marc Márquez at this weekend’s MotoGP Portuguese Grand Prix. | Listen to Pit Talk below. Mercedes suffered from it in 2022. Red Bull Racing initially did too, though it rebounded quickly after having got the fundamentals right. McLaren and Ferrari will both have institutional memory of having fallen so badly off the boil in 2009 after their titanic title struggle of 2008. Now McLaren and Red Bull Racing find themselves in this familiar position. Red Bull Racing knew going into the season that it was likely to be a step behind. It was so befuddled by its downward spiral after having dominated in 2023 that it willingly committed development time to last year’s car as a troubleshooting exercise to ensure its tools were working as expected. It ended up powering Verstappen to within two points of the championship. McLaren was therefore forced to switch focus back to last year’s car to ensure one of its drivers got over the line. Though it didn’t bring any major upgrades, every day spent squeezing pace from the car was a day not dedicated to doing the same for the 2026 machine. Unsurprisingly, these two top teams found their feet in 2026 eventually, albeit too late to stop Mercedes from running away with the championship. Development trajectory, frontrunners Red Bull Racing: improving by 0.037s per race Ferrari: improving by 0.020s per race McLaren: improving by 0.012s per race Mercedes: degrading by 0.007s per race McLaren hit its straps first, in Hungary, the Netherlands and Spain, taking three poles and two wins in four races. Red Bull Racing, though, surged forward with an upgrade in Azerbaijan that got Verstappen within 0.196s of victory. He then won in Malaysia, Singapore and Mexico, and he would have been a good chance to win in Brazil had he not started from the back. McLaren, though, hasn’t kept up in that time. In what Andrea Stella described as upgrade “ping-pong”, his team has slipped backwards as others have brought upgrades — just as McLaren had done in Hungary, setting off its run of big results. Gap to fastest, last five rounds (dry) Mercedes: +0.126s Red Bull Racing: +0.266s Ferrari: +0.308s McLaren: +0.496s This would certainly suggest that third place is a done deal for Red Bull Racing. Brazil looked more like an aberration given the wet conditions and Verstappen’s strong performance regardless. But McLaren has one more bullet in the chamber. McLAREN WON’T MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE TWICE Similar to last year, the final phase of this season is being defined by which team is still upgrading its car. Mercedes’s upgrade plan has been the most novel, with just two big packages — in Canada and then in Malaysia — brought to the car. It made that choice based on its available spend within the budget cap. It had already spent big during the off-season preparing the car for launch, so it had to be wiser and more targeted about when it would commit to building parts. Red Bull Racing blew its budget early in the season because its car was in such a parlous state in the opening rounds. By the time it got to Azerbaijan in September, it admitted its 2026 development program had hit the end of the road. McLaren, though, has been more miserly, spreading out its developments throughout the year — so much so that it’s still upgrading the car now, with the end of the season on the horizon. In Brazil the team bought new front and rear wings as well as new parts to the floor. The front wing in particular was interesting as a departure from its previous philosophy. The team said it was designed with the 2027 car in mind. Notably, the drivers seemed to review that the car had become less knife-edge in the way it handled, having become increasingly peaky through the rounds prior. Now, in Las Vegas, McLaren is bringing more new parts, which McLaren boss Andrea Stella said would “form the foundation” for next year’s car. Perhaps it’s for that reason that these final rounds of 2026 have more at stake for McLaren. If these new parts are fundamental to next year’s car, underperformance will give the feeling of a lack of momentum heading into 2027. “We'll do our best to make sure it goes down to the wire and in our favour,” McLaren racing director Randy Singh told the F1 Nation podcast. “We're treating it like a mini championship on our side. “It doesn’t feel [like] any less pressure than the last couple of season finales, to be honest. We've got three races as well, which is quite nice because we've got plenty of time to try and harvest as many points as we can. “This week everyone's pretty intense with seeing what we can learn from the last race — both in the dry and in the mixed conditions — and what we can do to prepare for Vegas.” BUT IS THIS THE TRACK TO PROVE IT? The circumstances won’t be helped this weekend, however, by the circuit. Las Vegas is a true bogey track for McLaren. The car was woefully uncompetitive at the first race and then well off the boil at the second. It was in better form last year, with Norris taking pole and finishing second, but then both cars were disqualified for technical infringements. Las Vegas historical top scorers Mercedes: 86 points Red Bull Racing: 76 points Ferrari: 69 points McLaren: 18 points It’s hard to have higher expectations for McLaren this season. On paper Las Vegas is not a friendly track for the orange car. The MCL40 is at its best through high-speed corners. It’s no good down straights, where its short gears and low aero efficiency are punished. It’s also been uncompetitive all year through short, slow corners. The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is all short, slow corners and the long back straight down Las Vegas Boulevard. Some of this weekend’s upgrades are designed to boost efficiency, but it would still be a surprise to see McLaren among the leading contenders. Whether or not it can get ahead of Red Bull Racing, however, is more important than whether or not it can win. “We all see it as a challenge and a big opportunity for us to really go and get a result at a circuit that we haven't had a good result at yet,” Singh said. “We're really approaching it from that underdog sense of we've not had a good one there, but we've got a good chance to have a really good result there [this year]. “We had the car in a good window in Brazil. We need to try and make sure we do the same in Vegas. “We've got a lot of work to do to try and make sure that we hit the ground running, and that we keep optimising the package as it is now.” CAN PIASTRI MAKE THE DIFFERENCE? There’s a secondary element to this battle: the second drivers. While Verstappen and Norris have three wins apiece, Oscar Piastri and Isack Hadjar are the only frontrunners yet to take the top step of the podium. Piastri has just two podiums for the entire season, the last of which came all the way back in Miami in May. Hadjar’s third-place finish in Brazil brought him up to three for the season. Piastri is 94 points behind Norris (246–152 points, 62–38 per cent), while Hadjar — who missed three rounds through injury — is 157 points behind Verstappen (279–122 points, 70–30 per cent). In percentage terms, only rookie Arvid Lindblad, the dismissed Esteban Ocon and son-of-the-owner Lance Stroll are further adrift of their teammates by points. Piastri’s difficulties adjusting to the new regulations have been well ventilated. Hadjar’s situation is different but similarly clear, this being just his second Formula 1 season and his first at Red Bull Racing. But given Verstappen and Norris can be assumed to have got the most out of their cars, how much could a big result from either swing the battle for third? Hadjar was very strong in Las Vegas last year, qualifying eighth and finishing sixth at a strong weekend for Racing Bulls. Piastri was unspectacular. Notwithstanding that he could have qualified on the front row without some badly timed yellow flags, in the race he ended up stuck behind the superbly defensive Andrea Kimi Antonelli, locking him out of a podium finish — though he was disqualified afterwards anyway. With Red Bull Racing likely to be the stronger performer this weekend, this could be a chance for Hadjar to deliver a significant blow for his team. The next race, though, could be Piastri’s chance to hit back. Qatar, replete with high-speed bends, should be McLaren territory, and it’s by far Piastri’s strongest circuit. Piastri has never finished off the podium in Lusail, and despite never having won the race — though he would have done so easily last year were it not for McLaren’s pit stop blunder — he has a career-best average finish of 2.3. He’s never been beaten by his teammate in a race. Including sprints, he’s taking home on average 22.3 points per weekend. Assuming Formula 1 makes it to Qatar, this will be the decisive weekend to McLaren’s hopes of finishing third — and to Piastri’s contribution to that effort. Abu Dhabi is then unlikely to play to McLaren’s strengths, particularly with Max Verstappen having won five of the last six grands prix at Yas Marina. Despite being the reigning champion, McLaren is the underdog in this battle. But with an eye on 2027, it hopes it won’t be the underdog again next season. The 2026 regulations have left many drivers struggling to find their feet and match the competitive pace they saw under the downforce era. Vegas will also see McLaren introduce a new floor, building on the upgrades that they brought in Brazil, which featured a new front wing. The steps the team has taken delivered immediate results, with Lando Norris keeping ahead of the field to claim another victory. "We will also have some solutions to improve drag during the Free Practice sessions, which we will then review before making a decision on whether to run them on Friday. "With plenty of opportunities to exploit the car's potential, both through evaluating the new upgrades and refining how to operate the package at the maximum potential available, the priority is to turn those learnings into performance on track and valuable points in the immediate term." McLaren were the only member of F1's 'big four' teams to bring upgrades to Brazil, where the new parts helped Norris win the Sao Paulo Grand Prix. Ross Hood, McLaren executive director of programme delivery, said: "Our programme delivery has evolved throughout this year and continues to do so. "The new regulations, combined with the volume and pace of performance coming from the tunnel and engineering through to the circuit, have made it an intense year. That galvanises the team and brings us closer together, so we get the right performance to the track while challenging each other and our ideas. "A new floor is arriving in Las Vegas this week, and it's a great example of our programme delivery. Oscar Piastri's 2026 Formula 1 struggles have shocked many, but team boss Zak Brown believes the new regulations have neutralised his competitive advantages. This season has been a difficult pill to swallow for Piastri. The Australian finds himself down in seventh, 94 points behind his team-mate Lando Norris in sixth. Whilst McLaren have also endured a difficult season thus far, Norris has enjoyed three victories and six podiums so far. Compared to Piastri's zero wins and 2 podiums in the same span. This dip in form has raised questions surrounding the 25-year-old. Some suggest he is experiencing a 'championship hangover,' following an intense battle last season. Despite leading the championship for the longest stint last season, Piastri fell short in the final rounds, finishing the season 13 points behind his team-mate in third, However, the McLaren driver explained that his form this season is due to adjusting to a new driving style. As F1 introduced new regulations, drivers across the grid found themselves learning different driving techniques required to finesse this rule set. This, according to Piastri, has led to a new 'adaptation process.' “The biggest thing has probably been the general driving style you have. Or that what you need is quite different for this year’s car compared to previous years,” Piastri explained via the F1 website. “Even in previous years, there’s been an element of adaptation and learning for that. But I think [it’s been a] combination of a few different things this year. “Obviously, the cars are smaller, the tyres are quite different. It means you really have to drive the car on the edge all of the time..." “So, it’s felt quite different to previous [cars] I’ve driven in general. That’s been quite an adaptation process. And learning to trust the car and retrain what feels like the limit is never an easy thing to try to adapt." Zak Brown highlights 2026 neutralisation as behind Oscar Piastri's dip Brown has echoed Piastri's assessment, suggesting the new regulations have changed the competitive order across the grid and taken away some of his driver's key advantages. Speaking on Sky Sports' F1 Show, the McLaren CEO pointed to the changing fortunes of several driver pairings, including Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton at Ferrari, as well as George Russell and Kimi Antonelli at Mercedes. “I think we’ve seen it mix up a little bit of the grid, right," Brown stated. “Charles [Leclerc] last year got the better of Lewis [Hamilton, at Ferrari]. Lewis is getting the better of him [now]. George [Russell] got the better of Kimi [Antonelli, last year at Mercedes]. I think it’s mixed up the grid a little bit.” The McLaren boss also identified a significant change in how Piastri's driving strengths translate to the new-generation cars. “I think if you look at Oscar’s strengths, they were kind of big, brave corners. Now all of a sudden these new big, brave corners, it’s like, hey, lift, conserve, preserve. So I think there’s a small element of him having to adapt to a new car.” Despite acknowledging Piastri's difficulties, Brown was quick to praise Norris, believing the reigning champion is currently performing at the highest level of his career. “And then, let’s not take any credit away from Lando. I’ve never seen him drive better,” the American continued. “So I think you have a combination of Lando, who’s driving the best I’ve ever seen him drive, [and] Oscar, who’s not yet clicked with it. McLaren's Oscar Piastri will exceed his internal combustion engine (ICE) allocation at the upcoming Las Vegas Grand Prix, resulting in a 10-place grid penalty for the Australian driver. Piastri will be receiving his fifth ICE of the season. Under the power-unit allocation rules, each driver can only receive four ICEs without receiving a sporting penalty. Taking a fifth, which is the first infringement, triggers a 10-place grid penalty. The positive outlook for him is that the Las Vegas Strip Circuit presents multiple overtaking opportunities. Piastri can attack on the circuit's long straights, especially if McLaren's recent upgrade packages [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/mclaren-f1-team-advances-preparations-for-2027-season] work well. PIASTRI'S RECENT STRUGGLES It has been a rough campaign this year for Piastri. From winning races and fighting for the championship in 2025, the 25-year-old has been on the back foot in terms of pace and consistency this season. He has only scored 152 points this year, which is 94 points behind his teammate, Lando Norris. Norris has also won three races and achieved six podiums in 2026. On the other hand, Piastri has not won yet, and he only has two podium finishes: a P2 in Japan and a P3 in Miami. The Miami Grand Prix was held back in the early days of May. That's how much of a struggle it has been for Piastri, especially in recent times. In the Mexican Grand Prix on November 1, the Australian driver also received a 10-second time penalty [https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/piastri-loses-p7-after-being-handed-post-race-penalty-at-mexico-city-gp.5dk3wHeak2yu7xWF0OhsRt] for causing a collision with Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad. From a P7 finish, the penalty dropped him outside the points. There's also the fact that Piastri has not advanced to the final session of qualifying in the last two races. He trails Norris in qualifying head-to-head, 13-7. BUILDING MOMENTUM IN THE LAST THREE RACES There's no way that Piastri can chase his teammate for sixth place in the Drivers' Standings. With 30 points over Red Bull's Isack Hadjar, Piastri might already be locked into seventh place. So, the Australian's focus in the three remaining races (if Qatar and Abu Dhabi push through) is to build momentum for next year. Former Haas team principal Guenther Steiner recently said [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/steiner-raises-the-alarms-piastri-does-not-have-his-seat-assured] that Piastri can't struggle like this again in 2027. If he does, McLaren boss Zak Brown might look for a replacement. items.article_search_text: The former German driver points to Liam Lawson and Oliver Bearman as the ideal candidates to occupy the Australian's seat if his performance does not improve. Günther Steiner has launched a warning that shakes up the driver market. The former Haas boss considers that Oscar Piastri could be living his last months at McLaren if he does not reverse his results crisis and has already put on the table the names of the drivers who in his opinion, would fit perfectly in the Australian's seat. It is not about Carlos Sainz with whom McLaren already worked in the past but about two young talents called to mark an era: Liam Lawson and Oliver Bearman. Steiner was clear when analyzing the situation: "If next year he has another season like this one, you're right. Zak will look for the next Oscar, I mean he will have to find him but maybe Liam Lawson [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/f1-racing-bulls-finally-confirm-lawson-and-lindblad-for-2027]is free. Zak will look for someone younger, we all know that Zak is quite good at discovering young talents and Zak also likes to sign them cheap. He is someone quite ruthless when it comes to changing drivers" he explained on the The Red Flags podcast. The phrase summarizes the philosophy of Zak Brown, McLaren's CEO: bet on emerging talent, before it becomes a consolidated star and do it at a reasonable price. Lando Norris Backs Potential F1 Return to Argentina: “It Would Be Incredible” [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/115ee240-4551-45ac-a981-a901c9fb7cbf.jpeg] Lando Norris Backs Potential F1 Return to Argentina: “It Would Be Incredible” The Briton is excited about the possibility of Formula 1 returning to Argentine soil in the coming years. He highlights the warmth of the region's public and assures that he would love to be part of a race in the country. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/lando-norris-backs-potential-f1-return-to-argentina-it-would-be-incredible] The first name on the list is Liam Lawson. The New Zealander who has signed an exceptional 2026 season with Racing Bulls, is the driver who best embodies the profile McLaren is looking for, his adaptability, his aggressiveness on track and his consistency have made him one of the most coveted drivers on the grid. His performance in the last races with three consecutive seventh places and a memorable comeback in Mexico from the pit lane, demonstrate that he has the necessary level to compete in a top team. However his recent renewal with Racing Bulls for 2027 complicates any short-term move, even so Steiner mentions him as a future option, aware that the driver market is volatile and that opportunities can arise when least expected. The second name is Oliver Bearman: the Briton current Haas [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/haas]driver and Ferrari academy member, has demonstrated notable progress in his second full season. With 23 points an aggressive but mature driving style and a learning capacity that has impressed friends and strangers alike, Bearman represents that mix of youth and talent that Brown values so much. His link with Ferrari could be an obstacle but his contract with Haas ends in 2027 and his long-term future is far from defined, for Steiner he is an ideal candidate for a team seeking to build long-term and his youth fits perfectly with McLaren's philosophy. Ollie Bearman Opens Up: “They Were Three Horrible Weeks” [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/3240dcf9-fa2a-4264-b415-4134d33d6c2c.jpeg] Ollie Bearman Opens Up: “They Were Three Horrible Weeks” The Briton finished seventeenth in Brazil and admits that he needs to disconnect after a triple header marked by the retirements in Austin and Mexico and a slow stop in Interlagos. [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/ollie-bearman-opens-up-they-were-three-horrible-weeks] Steiner's reflection also rules out other options that had been strongly rumored, when asked about the possibility of reuniting Lando Norris with Carlos Sainz, the German was blunt: he does not believe it is the most likely option: "Zak will look for someone younger" he insisted. The logic is simple: McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren]does not need a consolidated driver who charges a high salary and who has no room for growth, it needs a young talent with hunger and with potential to continue evolving and of course Lawson and Bearman fit that profile and Steiner knows it. Guenther Steiner, former Haas boss and one of the most listened-to analysts in the paddock, has launched a warning that can be interpreted as a notice to navigators: if the Australian repeats in 2027 a campaign like this year's, his future at McLaren [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/mclaren]could be in serious danger: "If he has another year like this next year, Zak will look for the next Oscar" Steiner sentenced on the The Red Flags podcast. The phrase, pronounced with the frankness that characterizes the Italian puts the focus on an uncomfortable reality for Piastri: his performance has been far below expectations. In 2025 he fought for the title until the end against his teammate Lando Norris but this year he is seventh with 152 points, light years from Max Verstappen's 279 or George Russell's 262. While Kimi Antonelli was crowned champion in Mexico, the Australian witnessed a season of ups and downs, with two podiums but without victories and with a manifest inability to adapt to the MCL40. F1 Daily: Piastri Splits From Webber, Drivers Complain to Pirelli, and Vandoorne Joins Jaguar [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/693cf553-3bd5-48e8-b6d3-fbfc3c0210e5.jpeg] F1 Daily: Piastri Splits From Webber, Drivers Complain to Pirelli, and Vandoorne Joins Jaguar Oscar Piastri has just made a major career move. In that context he mentioned names like that of Liam Lawson, who has just renewed with Racing Bulls or that of Oliver Bearman, Haas's great promise, Steiner's warning is not gratuitous: Brown has a reputation for being relentless when it comes to driver decisions, and Piastri [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/oscar-piastri-makes-major-career-move-what-it-means-for-his-f1-future]knows it. At 25 years old the Australian is at a crossroads, his contract with McLaren extends until 2028, but contracts in Formula 1 are as solid as the results that back them. Piastri has talent to spare as he demonstrated last year, but the irregularity of the MCL40 and his difficulty in finding the car's operating window have taken their toll. His teammate, Norris, has won three races and has scored 246 points, a difference of 94 units that reflects the gap between the two. F1 Business Weekly: Haas Adds a Bank Sponsor, F1's Billion-Dollar Revenue, and Apple's Free Las Vegas Coverage [https://deweb-519a7.b-cdn.net/post-images/9be9d8a1-933e-445d-ba38-98b724bc0e81.jpeg] F1 Business Weekly: Haas Adds a Bank Sponsor, F1's Billion-Dollar Revenue, and Apple's Free Las Vegas Coverage Haas is adding a banking giant to their list of sponsors. McLaren expects a competitive car for next season and the Australian will have to demonstrate that he can fight for victories again, if he does not, Steiner's words could become prophecy. Zak Brown is not known for his infinite patience and the driver market always has names willing to occupy a seat in a top team. Piastri is warned, the pressure does not only come from outside: his own teammate, Lando Norris, has demonstrated this year that he can carry the weight of the team and score victories even when the car is not up to the task. That constant comparison is a reminder of what McLaren expects from him, the talent is there but consistency and adaptability will mark the difference between consolidating himself as a leader or becoming a promise that never fully exploded. Read more at foxsports.com.au Oscar Piastri’s fourth season has fallen short of lofty standards set by 2025, but the Australian says this year’s struggles come with a silver lining for 2027. Oscar Piastri will look back on 2026 feeling positive about his rate improvement rather than dwelling on his lack of results. Piastri, a championship contender to the final round of last year, has not kicked on in 2026, when sweeping rule changes have thrown him off his game. The Australian has been decisively behind teammate Lando Norris, the reigning champion, for most of the season, even if the margins have been relatively small. Fox Sports, available on Kayo Sports, is the only place to watch every practice, qualifying session and race in the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship™ LIVE in 4K | Get Kayo now > McLaren’s relative lack of competitiveness for much of the year has been an additional difficulty, though Piastri has been a step behind Norris at the few rounds at which the car has been a genuine victory threat. But McLaren has seen signs of progress from the Australian as the year has progressed, and in Singapore last month CEO Zak Brown said Piastri was fundamentally back to where he was in 2025 in terms of his confidence with the car despite few headline results to show for it. As just one example, despite finishing sixth in Brazil behind the victorious Norris, Piastri’s race pace was respectable for much of the grand prix. Though he admitted 2026 has “definitely been tough”, Piastri told the F1 website that he was finding joy in “trying to make progress”. “I've always tried to remove results from what success looks like,” he said. “Of course results do help, but especially when you're not in a position to win races — whether it be because of the car or the kind of struggles I've had this year — sometimes a win and a successful weekend looks like improvement rather than perfection. “That's brought me joy for sure. There's been some very strong weekends this year that I've been really happy with. [I’m] just trying to work through those things.” The contrast between Piastri and Norris this season has been stark, particularly at the weekends when more has been up for grabs, with the Englishman rarely dropping an opportunity this year. However, it’s been clear from early on that there would be little on the line for McLaren and its drivers this year. Mercedes’s strong start all but guaranteed both titles, even if the field has closed during the year. The team is fourth in the standings and chasing Red Bull Racing for third, while Norris and Piastri are unlikely to finish higher or lower than sixth and seventh respectively in the drivers championship. The team’s step down under new regulations has been a blessing in disguise for Piastri, who has had a chance to do his learning without the pressure of needing to contend for a title in the hope that he’ll be ready for a championship challenge next year if circumstances allow. The same applies to some of the weaknesses that undermined his 2025 campaign later in the year. “Even some of the challenges from last year, they weren't completely dissimilar to what I've got this year, and I feel like I've definitely made a lot of progress on that in general,” he said. “These last few races are definitely going to be another challenge in terms of testing where I'm at, in terms of developing those skills. “Having that challenge has been tough, obviously, but getting through it and then continuing to work on it [is] ultimately going to be rewarding and [will] hopefully set me up for whatever car we get [in future]. “Definitely between myself and the pretty close and intimate engineering team around me, we've learned a lot about each other and how we get the most out of ourselves [as well as] how we get more out of ourselves. "That's been a good process to go through for sure.” Oscar Piastri vs Lando Norris, 2026 so far Qualifying head to head: Norris leads 13-7 Qualifying differential: Norris ahead 1.7 places Time differential: Norris faster by 0.111s (dry only) Race head to head: Norris leads 10-4 Race differential: Norris ahead 1.9 places Race pace differential: Norris faster by 0.3s Points: Norris leads 246-152 (62–38 per cent) Some of the changes to the cars this season have played into Piastri’s weaknesses. The cars are generally lower in grip given the reduced aerodynamic load, and the Australian is at his best when he can exploit high-grip conditions. Further, though, is the way the 2026 car wants to be hustled. Whereas in previous seasons Piastri has been able to achieve a car’s peak performance by driving fractionally below the limit, this year’s car prefers to be pushed to or beyond the limit at all times to deliver its best. Piastri isn’t as comfortable reacting to a peaky car — and the problem has been exacerbated by McLaren’s 2026 challenger being particularly unpredictable at the limit, as even Norris has complained. “You really have to drive the car on the edge all of the time — certainly our car, I don't know what others think of it,” he said. “You're always driving on the edge to an extent, but this year it's really always taking you beyond the edge of trying to salvage things. It's felt quite different to previous [cars] and even a lot of the previous cars I've driven in general. “That's been quite an adaptation process, and learning to trust the car and retrain what feels like the limit is never an easy thing to try and adapt. “It's been tougher than I expected with trying to get to grips with the car … it's definitely thrown in a lot of challenges, and I feel like I've had to change a lot of things in how I drive or certainly tweak things. “But I feel I'm making some progress now in the second half of this year, so [I’m] just trying to continue that.” MORE FORMULA 1 'DID IT FOR AUSTRALIA': How Ricciardo’s ‘bogan’ act came to define his F1 wins... and the ‘loose’ history that inspired it SILLY SEASON: Final piece left in F1's 2027 driver puzzle as Red Bull finally makes contract call 'NOT THE REALITY': Alarming truth about F1's 'new dynasty' claims... and what it means for 2027 Though third in the constructors championship will be of limited consolation to the team that won the last two titles — notwithstanding the boost in prize money — the final three weekends of the season are critical to Piastri and McLaren preparing for a 2027 both hope will bring far bigger prizes. “Everyone is still very determined to get back to where we know we can be,’ Piastri said. “I think we're on our way back there; development and upgrades have always been a strong point for us, and hopefully we can just keep pushing. “The teams around us have definitely raised the bar, but I know that we can raise it even higher.” Oscar Piastri splits from F1 legend manager Mark Webber Motorsport: Liam Lawson will remain with Racing Bulls for the 2027 Formula 1 season alongside teammate Arvid Lindblad after the team confirms its unchanged driver line-up.
